title: FDA Acceptance of Foreign Clinical Data Not Conducted Under an IND: 21 CFR 312.120, 314.106 and Approval Precedents
summary: How FDA judges non-IND foreign clinical studies under 21 CFR 312.120 and 314.106, with approvals and CRLs showing when ex-US data sufficed.
body_markdown:
## How FDA evaluates foreign clinical data not conducted under an IND: 21 CFR 312.120, 314.106 and the approval precedents


### Key takeaways


- FDA asks two separate questions about ex-US data. The first is whether a foreign study not conducted under an IND is acceptable as support at all (21 CFR 312.120: GCP, IEC review, informed consent, and FDA's ability to validate the data)[280](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-312.120)[281](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-312.120)[282](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-312.120) . The second, which applies only when foreign data are the sole basis for approval, is whether those data apply to the U.S. population and U.S. medical practice, came from investigators of recognized competence, and can be validated (21 CFR 314.106(b))[276](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-314.106) .
- A study that fails 312.120 is not accepted as support for an IND or marketing application unless FDA grants a waiver. FDA will still examine its data[283](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-312.120)[91](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=91) .
- The precedents show that entirely or predominantly foreign packages can support approval. Coartem, Loqtorzi (toripalimab) and Bylvay (odevixibat) are examples[416](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=416)[421](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=421)[364](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=364)[388](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=388) . They fail when U.S. applicability is not shown: a single-country population, a comparator or endpoint that does not match U.S. care, or no unmet need to justify flexibility. Sintilimab, the January 2024 penpulimab CRL and the DREAMM-8 regimen of Blenrep illustrate this[130](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=130)[131](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=131)[518](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=518)[429](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=429)[336](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=336) .
- FDA's September 2024 draft oncology guidance prefers multiregional clinical trials (MRCTs) with meaningful U.S. enrollment. Flexibility is reserved mainly for diseases that are rare in the U.S. or concentrated in other regions[145](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=145)[518](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=518)[362](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=362) .


### Two regulatory gates: acceptability versus sole-basis approval


#### 21 CFR 312.120: acceptance of foreign non-IND studies


Under 312.120(a), FDA will accept a well-designed and well-conducted foreign clinical study not conducted under an IND as support for an IND or a marketing application under FD&C Act section 505 or PHS Act section 351, if the study meets these conditions[280](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-312.120) :


- **Good clinical practice.** The study must follow GCP, a standard for design, conduct, monitoring, auditing, recording, analysis and reporting that assures credible data and protects subjects[280](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-312.120) .
- **Independent ethics committee review.** An IEC must approve the study or give a favorable opinion before it starts, and must continue to review it[281](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-312.120) .
- **Informed consent.** Freely given consent must be obtained and documented before the study starts. A narrow exception covers life-threatening situations where the IEC finds, before the study starts, that consent is not feasible and either that the conditions are consistent with 21 CFR 50.23 or 50.24(a) or that protocol measures will protect subjects' rights, safety and well-being[281](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-312.120)[282](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-312.120) .
- **Data validation.** FDA must be able to validate the data through an onsite inspection if it considers one necessary. The rule requires that FDA be able to inspect. It does not require an inspection in every case[282](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-312.120) .


Under 312.120(b), the sponsor must describe how it ensured GCP conformity. The supporting information covers[285](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-312.120)[286](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-312.120)[287](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-312.120)[288](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-312.120)[289](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-312.120)[290](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-312.120)[291](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-312.120)[292](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-312.120)[293](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-312.120)[294](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-312.120)[295](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-312.120) :


1. The investigator's qualifications.
2. A description of the research facilities.
3. A detailed protocol and results summary, plus case records or background data if FDA asks for them.
4. A description of the drug substance and drug product used, including components, formulation, specifications and, if available, bioavailability.
5. For effectiveness claims, evidence that the study is adequate and well controlled under 21 CFR 314.126.
6. The IEC's name, address and a statement that it meets the 21 CFR 312.3 definition.
7. A summary of the IEC's decision.
8. How informed consent was obtained.
9. Any incentives offered to subjects.
10. How the sponsor monitored the study and ensured protocol compliance.
11. How investigators were trained in GCP and the protocol, and whether written commitments to comply were obtained.


Under 312.120(c), the sponsor may request a waiver of any requirement in (a)(1) or (b). The request must explain why compliance is unnecessary or cannot be achieved, propose an alternative, or give another justification. FDA may grant a waiver in the interest of public health[296](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-312.120)[297](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-312.120) . Records must be kept for 2 years after FDA's decision on the marketing application[298](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-312.120) , or, if the study supports an IND but not a marketing application, for 2 years after the IND submission.


#### 21 CFR 314.106: foreign data as the sole basis for approval


Section 312.120 points to 21 CFR 314.106 for approval based solely on foreign clinical data[301](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-312.120) . Under 314.106(b), FDA may approve an NDA on foreign data alone only if all three conditions are met[276](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-314.106) :


1. The data are applicable to the U.S. population and U.S. medical practice.
2. Investigators of recognized competence conducted the studies.
3. The data can be considered valid without an FDA onsite inspection, or FDA can validate them through inspection or other appropriate means.


If any criterion is not met, the application cannot be approved on foreign data alone. FDA applies the policy flexibly according to the drug and the data[276](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-314.106) . FDA encourages a presubmission meeting with any applicant that intends to rely only on foreign data[277](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-314.106) .


#### How FDA guidance applies the rule


FDA's final guidance *FDA Acceptance of Foreign Clinical Studies Not Conducted Under an IND: Frequently Asked Questions* (March 2012) explains 312.120. It states that running a foreign study under an IND is optional, and that foreign studies run under an IND must meet IND requirements unless those are waived[53](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=53)[80](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=80) . The FAQ recommends that applications state clearly[83](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=83) :


- whether each study had foreign sites only or both foreign and U.S. sites;
- whether each foreign site operated under an IND or under 312.120;
- where each supporting-information element and any 312.120(c) waiver request can be found.


ICH E3 and E6 documentation can help meet these requirements. However, neither is mandatory, and following them may still leave gaps under 312.120[85](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=85) .


Two other FDA guidances address data validation. FDA's guidance on electronic health record data says that if the necessary records do not exist, FDA may not accept the study. If records exist but foreign law prohibits their disclosure, the sponsor can request a 312.120(c) waiver. FDA and the sponsor must then agree on another way to validate the data before FDA relies on it[86](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=86)[87](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=87) . FDA's guidance on clinical investigator inspections says international inspections usually focus on studies that are critical to approval decisions, including foreign non-IND sites. For those sites, an inspection can help decide whether the study met 312.120[89](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=89) .


#### Device parallel: 21 CFR 812.28 and 814.15


The device framework mirrors the drug framework. Under 21 CFR 812.28, FDA accepts data from device investigations conducted outside the U.S. if three conditions are met[264](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-812.28)[265](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-812.28)[266](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-812.28)[267](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-812.28) :


- the investigation followed GCP, including IEC review and informed consent;
- the required supporting information is submitted or available;
- FDA can validate the data when it considers validation necessary.


The amount of supporting information required depends on whether the device is significant risk, non-significant risk, or exempt[269](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-812.28)[270](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-812.28)[271](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-812.28) . Section 812.28(e) also lets FDA accept data that do not meet these conditions if FDA believes the results are credible and accurate and subjects were adequately protected[273](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-812.28) . For PMAs, 21 CFR 814.15(b) applies the same three sole-basis criteria as 314.106[173](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-814.15)[174](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-814.15)[175](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-814.15)[176](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-814.15) .


### The applicability question: what FDA guidance expects


Most foreign-data disputes turn on applicability rather than GCP. FDA's guidance positions are:


- **Postmarketing approaches for underrepresented populations (draft, August 2023).** When most patients were enrolled outside the U.S., the sponsor should submit data and a rationale showing that the results apply to U.S. patients. FDA may request or require further studies in relevant U.S. subpopulations[158](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=158) .
- **Oncology multiregional clinical development programs (draft, September 2024).** The paramount consideration is whether the data apply to the intended U.S. population and U.S. standard oncology care. Low U.S. enrollment limits FDA's ability to assess whether the treatment effect is consistent across regions[143](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=143) . Sponsors should plan enough U.S. enrollment for a robust assessment and should use control arms that reflect U.S. standard of care[145](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=145)[149](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=149) . MRCT data can support approval if they apply to U.S. patients and practice. FDA weighs both intrinsic and extrinsic factors[159](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=159) .
- **ICH E5 (1998).** A full development program does not need to be repeated in each new region[160](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=160) . Foreign data can make up most or all of a clinical package, sometimes with a bridging study[165](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=165) . A product may not need bridging data if it is ethnically insensitive and medical practice is similar[163](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=163) . A controlled bridging trial is called for when differences in concomitant or adjunct therapy could change efficacy or safety[164](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=164) .
- **ICH E17 (2018).** E17 is intended to increase regulatory acceptance of MRCTs as primary evidence for approval and should be used together with E5[166](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=166) .


### Precedents where ex-US data supported approval


Product Foreign-data profile How FDA resolved applicability and data validity Outcome


Coartem (artemether/lumefantrine), NDA 022268 The NDA contained only foreign studies, with no U.S. IND development[416](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=416) The inspected sites generally followed GCP. The Chinese site had no significant violations and the other sites had only minor ones, so FDA concluded their data could support the indication[417](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=417)[421](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=421) . One site's investigator had a credentialing issue, but FDA still judged that site's data acceptable[418](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=418)[420](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=420) Approved April 7, 2009, for acute, uncomplicated *P. falciparum* malaria in patients weighing 5 kg or more[464](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=464)[486](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=486)[488](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=488)


Loqtorzi (toripalimab-tpzi), BLA 761240 JUPITER-02 efficacy population was entirely of Chinese ethnicity[363](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=363) FDA reviewed the application under 314.106(b)[360](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=360) . It allowed flexibility because NPC is rare in the U.S., unmet need was high, and the cisplatin-gemcitabine comparator was U.S. standard care[362](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=362) . FDA noted that keratinizing disease and U.S. diversity were underrepresented, and required a postmarketing commitment for more representative data[363](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=363)[364](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=364) . FDA conducted site inspections to validate the data[364](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=364) Approved October 27, 2023[337](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=337) . An earlier CRL (April 29, 2022) stated that clinical site inspections in China, delayed by COVID-19 travel restrictions, were required before approval[236](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=236)[255](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=255)[259](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=259)


Bylvay (odevixibat), NDA 215498 13% U.S. patients in the primary trial (8/62)[216](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=216) FDA accepted the foreign data because diagnoses were molecularly confirmed, severity criteria were prespecified, and standard-of-care differences were not expected to affect the primary endpoint[219](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=219) . It found no literature suggesting the results would not apply to U.S. patients[388](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=388) Approval recorded July 20, 2021[373](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=373)


Ensacove (ensartinib), NDA 218171 eXALT3 had about 4% U.S. enrollment (12 patients) and a crizotinib comparator[209](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=209)[322](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=322) FDA accepted crizotinib because it was an agreed, appropriate comparator when the trial began[320](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=320)[321](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=321) . FDA also relied on 185 patients of cumulative U.S. experience and on similar U.S. and non-U.S. outcomes[322](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=322)[323](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=323) . It noted that the trial was multiregional and run under an IND, and concluded the results applied to the U.S. population. Underrepresentation was handled through a postmarketing commitment[321](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=321) Traditional approval; NDA decision December 18, 2024[325](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=325)[317](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=317)


Zenbexus (iberdomide), NDA 221075 U.S. patients were 1.9% of the MRD primary analysis population and 5.1% of the ITT population[205](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=205)[206](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=206) FDA considered the broader ITT population, a supportive study with 44% U.S. enrollment, consistent subgroup results, and no PK differences by race or region[207](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=207) FDA concluded the totality of data supported U.S. applicability for accelerated approval[208](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=208)


These approvals share a pattern. In these approvals, FDA's reasoning typically turned on:


- the disease or setting justified flexibility, for example when it is rare in the U.S. or more common elsewhere[362](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=362) ;
- the comparator matched U.S. practice, or was acceptable at the time the trial began[362](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=362)[321](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=321) ;
- the data could be validated through inspection[421](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=421)[364](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=364) ;
- remaining representativeness gaps could be handled after approval through a postmarketing commitment[364](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=364)[321](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=321) .


### Precedents where ex-US data were not sufficient


Product Issue FDA position


Sintilimab + chemotherapy, first-line non-squamous NSCLC (ODAC, February 10, 2022) ORIENT-11 was conducted only in China[128](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=128)[129](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=129) FDA cited a younger, more often male, all-Asian population, and noted that a single-country trial cannot test whether results are consistent across regions[130](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=130) . It also found that the PFS endpoint and the comparator did not match U.S. practice[131](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=131)[132](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=132) . FDA concluded ORIENT-11 did not meet the foreign-data criteria of 312.120 and 314.106[516](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=516) . It said NSCLC, a common worldwide disease, should be studied in MRCTs, and that the drug did not address an unmet need warranting flexibility[518](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=518) . ODAC voted 14 to 1 that more trials showing U.S. applicability were needed before a regulatory decision[134](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=134)


Emtriva (emtricitabine), study FTC-302 South African trial that continued without a valid IND after a clinical hold[33](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=33)[35](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=35) FDA reviewed the study under 312.120. It found the study did not meet the ethical and host-country legal requirements and could not serve as a pivotal efficacy trial[35](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=35) . FDA still reviewed its safety data[458](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=458) . Approval rested on FTC-301A and FTC-303[459](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=459)


Penpulimab-kcqx (AK105), CRL January 19, 2024 NPC application[422](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=422) FDA asked for a multiregional randomized trial against an acceptable control, with PFS and OS endpoints and "an adequate representation of U.S. patients" reflecting the ethnically diverse NPC population[429](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=429)


Blenrep (belantamab mafodotin-blmf), DREAMM-8 regimen not approved October 23, 2025 (FDA approved the bortezomib-dexamethasone regimen that day on DREAMM-7) DREAMM-8[250](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=250) FDA cited "substantial concerns regarding the applicability of the DREAMM-8 study results to the current U.S. patient population," including a control arm that is not an approved U.S. regimen and limited U.S. enrollment[336](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=336)


Atropine 0.01% ophthalmic, CRLs August 27, 2025 (Vyluma) and October 22, 2025 (SYDNEXIS) Myopia programs supported in part by studies in Asian populations[423](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=423)[231](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=231) FDA found that the supportive studies and literature did not provide evidence in "the United States intended use population"[431](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=431) . In the other CRL, FDA questioned whether efficacy would generalize to a U.S. population that includes many non-Asian patients[254](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=254)


Glofitamab + GemOx, STARGLO (ODAC, May 20, 2025) U.S. enrollment was lower than expected[135](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=135) FDA presented its position on applicability to U.S. patients and practice[136](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=136) . It described inconsistent treatment effects between Asian and non-Asian regions, a potential survival detriment in the non-Asian region, and added uncertainty in the U.S. subgroup[97](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=97)


Toripalimab shows the contrast. Both toripalimab and penpulimab were NPC applications built mainly on data from Asia. FDA approved toripalimab after accepting its comparator and validating its data[362](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=362)[364](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=364) . For penpulimab, the January 2024 CRL requested a new multiregional trial with U.S. patients[429](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=429) . FDA later approved penpulimab-kcqx on April 23, 2025.


### Procedural precedents on 312.120 supporting information and waivers


- **Savaysa (edoxaban).** The sponsor asked to waive some 312.120(b) supporting information for foreign non-IND studies in the EU, China and Japan. FDA agreed only "providing that these studies do not contribute materially to your application"[43](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=43)[44](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=44) .
- **Byfavo (remimazolam).** The sponsor proposed using foreign non-IND studies in other indications to support the safety database. FDA asked for the reports, protocols, original data and a rationale for relevance and quality[46](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=46)[47](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=47) . FDA said the rationale appeared to contain the required 312.120 elements, but left open whether the data would support approval until the NDA review[49](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=49) .
- **Signifor (pasireotide).** At a Belgian site not run under an IND, FDA's inspection reviewer noted that no Form FDA 1572 was required, although the sponsor remained responsible for GCP compliance. The reviewer also found that a consent form allowing generic regulatory-authority access to records was sufficient, even though it did not name FDA[37](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=37)[39](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=39) .
- **Ongentys (opicapone).** The sponsor attested that the solely foreign Study 302 met GCP and 312.120[40](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=40)[42](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=42) . The reviewer called study conduct "very sloppy," but found that the database corrections did not change efficacy or safety conclusions[41](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=41) .
- **Treosulfan, CRL July 30, 2021.** FDA noted that the race variable was empty for every subject in Study MC-FludT.14/L II. FDA said this did not provide adequate information to show the results apply to the U.S. population, and listed the point as an additional comment rather than an approvability issue[237](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=237)[257](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=257)[258](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=258) .


### Practical implications for sponsors


1. **Satisfy 312.120 and 314.106 separately.** GCP, IEC and consent compliance, with data FDA can validate, make a foreign study admissible. They do not show that the data apply to U.S. patients. ORIENT-11 met its primary endpoint and still failed both the 312.120 and 314.106 criteria in FDA's assessment[516](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=516) .
2. **Make data validation possible.** Records must be available for FDA to inspect. Where foreign law blocks access, request a 312.120(c) waiver and agree on another validation method before submission[86](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=86)[87](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=87) . Delayed inspections held up the 2022 toripalimab action[255](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=255) .
3. **Match the comparator and endpoints to U.S. practice.** Control arms that are not U.S. standard of care were central to the sintilimab and Blenrep outcomes[131](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=131)[336](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=336) . FDA judges comparator appropriateness by the standard of care at the time the trial was designed[321](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=321) .
4. **Justify any flexibility.** FDA's flexibility depends on disease epidemiology and unmet need. It is less likely for common diseases with existing therapies[518](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=518)[362](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=362) .
5. **Plan for MRCTs with U.S. enrollment.** FDA's oncology guidance and its ODAC briefings treat prospectively planned MRCTs with sufficient U.S. participants as the preferred route under ICH E5 and E17[145](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=145)[513](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=513)[515](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=515)[520](https://rhizomeai.com/articles/fda-evaluates-foreign-clinical-data-not-conducted?showSourceNumber=520) .
6. **Use the presubmission meeting.** FDA encourages a presubmission meeting before any application that relies only on foreign data[277](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-314.106)[177](https://www.ecfr.gov/current/title-21/section-814.15) .
